CCDN THEOREM 3: FORMAL PROOF ROADMAP
=================================

Target: N_aff(X,B) <= C(n) d^3 B^(1/d) (log B + d), uniformly in X,
for n >= 2, integral affine curves over Q of degree d >= 1, and real B >= 1.

The rational-plane target PlaneCurveBound is now proved by SharpPlaneCount.
The full AffineCurveBound is now proved by AffineCurveBound.affineCurveBound.
The bounded projection and general-curve counting assembly are complete.
No external counting result is accepted as an axiom.
The completed-step history below records intermediate hypotheses; its finite-field
counting inputs are now discharged by SharpPlaneCount.sharpPlaneResidueBound.

Representation
--------------
Integer boxes use floor(B), with a proved equivalence to |x_i| <= B.
PlaneCurveBound uses irreducible rational bivariate polynomials and totalDegree.
AffineCurveBound uses prime ideals and eventual linear growth of the filtered
coordinate ring. HasAffineCurveDegree I d means dim(F_M(Q[x]/I)) = d*M+c for all
sufficiently large M. Each F_M is proved finite-dimensional and the slope is
proved unique. PlaneHilbert proves the exact principal-plane Hilbert-function
formula and total-degree comparison. The theorem uses this affine Hilbert-degree
interface directly; application-specific geometric degree correspondences
remain obligations of the application.

Completed prerequisite: Bombieri--Vaaler (CCDN Theorem 3.3.4)
---------------------------------------------------------
ArithmeticHeights.BombieriVaaler contains the small integer kernel vector theorem,
including the gcd of maximal minors. Its 25-module dependency is vendored from
rwst/Subspace-Theorems at 09835cb23557ae5ae0cf55a9c4ab9055f5d60338.
It has been rebuilt on Lean/Mathlib 4.35.0. Axioms.lean audits its exported
declarations and their transitive axiom dependencies.

Completed assembly steps
------------------------
1. A nonzero integer coefficient vector on distinct monomials gives a nonzero
   polynomial, with the expected degree and coefficient bounds.
2. Evaluation-matrix kernel vectors give vanishing polynomials. Rational row
   span transports vanishing from selected rows to the larger point set.
3. RowSelection now selects independent spanning rows from any finite matrix.
   A nonzero column annihilator proves that the row count is strictly less than
   the number of columns. Bombieri--Vaaler produces a small vanishing polynomial when the selected
   evaluation rows are independent and fewer than the available monomials.
4. A nonzero integer multiple has a leading coefficient at least as large in
   absolute value as the factor's. The explicit strict determinant threshold
   therefore implies nondivisibility. The threshold is NOT proved for curves.
5. The archimedean bound |det(A*A^T)| <= s! (N*H^2)^s and monomial bounds
   supply the upper-bound side of the determinant argument.
6. Cauchy--Binet yields determinant divisibility from weighted factorizations
   over any commutative ring. Repeated weights give an exponent at least
   s^2/(2*mu)-s. For univariate integer polynomial evaluations in one residue
   class the determinant and gcd of maximal minors are divisible by
   p^(s*(s-1)/2). SmoothLocalDeterminant constructs a common polynomial Newton
   approximation for all integral points of a smooth plane residue class,
   establishing this same exponent from the actual curve equation and a unit
   partial derivative. SmoothPlaneChart handles either derivative direction.
   SmoothReduction constructs the actual finite-field residue partition.
   SingularTangent bounds the actual origin-adic layers by the multiplicity of
   the reduced plane equation. Homogeneous generators and their integer lifts
   give a common approximation modulo every p^N at all actual integral zeros.
   SingularLocalDeterminant proves exponent sum_{i<s} floor(i/mu), and
   SingularPlaneChart proves translation, maximal-minor divisibility and
   residue-block assembly. No local spanning/factorization hypothesis remains.
   PlaneMultiplicity constructs the actual positive order at each reduced
   point and bounds it by the original integer equation degree.
   SingularReduction constructs the entire residue partition and total
   multiplicity M, proving M>0 and an exponent e with s^2<=2*M*(e+s),
   s^2/(2*M)-s<=e, and p^e dividing the maximal-minor gcd. The caller supplies
   only actual integral zeros and a nonzero reduced equation.
   Sharp finite-field counts with multiplicity remain open.
7. The real inequalities eliminating coefficient height, absorbing additive
   errors, specializing degrees 2..24, and absorbing logs are proved.
8. Distinct prime-power divisibilities combine into a product divisor and
   the associated logarithmic lower bound. MertensFirst proves the bounded
   error in sum_{p<=x} log(p)/p = log(x)+O(1), including the prime-power
   correction. PrimeSums proves the weighted lower bound when the residue
   multiplicity satisfies N_p <= p+C*sqrt(p), with an explicit excluded-prime
   charge. It combines this with the local exponents to prove the analytic
   determinant lower bound. The geometric N_p estimate, control of excluded
   primes remain to be proved. PrimeCutoff now bounds the prime-weighted tail
   by an absolute constant times L^(-1/2). SingularDeterminantCutoff uses
   L=27*d^4 to retain the required 4*log(d) degree loss.

Next major milestone: global determinant lower bound (Proposition 3.2.6)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
A. Local algebra and multiplicity: Section 2, especially Lemma 2.4 and
   Corollary 2.5. Construct the local-ring filtrations and establish the
   p-adic determinant valuation from their graded dimensions. This is now
   proved for arbitrary plane-curve residue points, including singular points,
   using the actual translated mod-p equation. Every graded layer has at most
   mu homogeneous generators, and finite-precision lifting gives the exponent
   sum_{i<s} floor(i/mu) >= s^2/(2*mu)-s. The singular plane local-algebra
   obligation is closed. The general higher-dimensional hypersurface version
   of CCDN Lemma 2.4 is not claimed; the plane counting route needs the case
   implemented here.
B. Aggregate residue classes (Proposition 2.6). The numerical convexity estimate
   preserving the leading constant and the resulting logarithmic prime-product
   lower bound are proved in ResidueAggregation. BlockDeterminant now proves
   the algebraic aggregation too: an integer column-lattice factorization and
   Cauchy--Binet combine all block minor divisors into a divisor of the full
   determinant and the gcd of maximal minors. No rank or nonempty-block
   assumptions are required. This aggregation obligation is closed.
C. Bound point counts with multiplicity over finite fields (Lemma 2.7).
   PlaneSingularities now proves the d(d-1) bound for distinct singular points
   when d is below the characteristic, including existence of a nonzero partial
   derivative. PlaneMultiplicitySmooth now bounds actual total multiplicity by
   the point count plus d^2(d-1), using the chosen local orders. The full point
   estimate remains open.
   For the plane-curve route only n=1 in the projective hypersurface argument
   is needed, but this still requires nontrivial finite-field geometry.
D. Bound bad primes using effective irreducibility/Noether forms (Section 3.2),
   including Ruppert's theorem as used in Theorem 3.2.2. Prove the required
   weighted prime-sum estimates rather than assuming them.
   BadPrimeCharge now supplies the analytic witness-to-charge step: for primes
   p>L dividing a positive integer D with log D<=L*H and H>=1,
   sum log(p)/p<=log H+2*mertensError+1. Its exponential factor is at most
   exp(2*mertensError+1)*H. This follows from Mertens on the lower interval
   and the product of distinct prime divisors on the upper interval. The
   plane geometric bad-prime criterion is now proved by the differential
   matrix construction below; no general-dimensional Noether-forms theorem is asserted.
   The differential core is now proved in AlgebraicDifferentialConstants,
   RationalDifferential, DifferentialResidue, RationalClosedForms and
   BivariateClosedForms. Formal differentiation on F(t) has exactly F as its
   constants in characteristic zero; algebraic extensions add no constants
   when F is algebraically closed. Differentiating the cleared closed-form
   equation at a simple root proves residue constancy without partial fractions.
   For monic irreducible f in F[x][y], strict y-degree bounds imply
   (P,Q)=a*(partial_y f,partial_x f), with a in F. Gauss's lemma, the root
   extension, its derivation and its constant field are all constructed.
   BivariateFactorForms gives actual closed forms from g*h and g^(k+2)*h,
   plus non-proportionality results under explicit coprimality hypotheses.
   BivariateCoefficientMatrix and ClosedFormBaseChange now construct the actual
   integer matrix on 2*d² coefficients, indexed by all output monomials, and
   prove compatibility with arbitrary coefficient maps. ClosedFormRank and
   FiniteRowMinor turn monic absolute irreducibility in characteristic zero
   into a nonzero integer minor of order 2*d²-1. ClosedFormIntegerMinor proves
   that characteristic-p rank drop forces p to divide this same determinant.
   ClosedFormHeight bounds entries by 2*d*H and r-minors by r!*(2*d*H)^r.
   ClosedFormMinorCharge puts its logarithmic height below
   27*d^4*(1+log(H)/d²), and proves the corresponding prime charge bound for
   primes where the actual matrix has rank drop. ClosedFormKernelWitness
   reconstructs grid-supported polynomial pairs and proves rank drop from two
   independent closed forms, in arbitrary characteristic.
   BivariateTotalDegree transports the exact multivariate total degree and
   proves that factor forms fit the coefficient grid. ClosedFormFactorRank and
   ClosedFormReducibility now establish the full positive-characteristic rank
   implication for monic equations with outer degree equal to total degree and
   smaller than the characteristic. A monic irreducible factor is extracted
   with its full multiplicity; the cofactor is proved coprime in the univariate
   fraction-field ring. The distinct- and repeated-factor forms supply the
   second independent kernel vector.
   MonicBadReduction therefore constructs a positive height-controlled integer
   divisible by every actual geometric bad prime above d for monic integer
   equations, and proves their log(1+log(H)/d²)+O(1) charge. Bad reduction is
   reducibility in the algebraic closure of ZMod p, not an assumed rank predicate.
   ClosedFormScaling removes integer monicity: normalize only over the
   coefficient field and preserve the rank of the original integer matrix.
   ConstantLeadingBadReduction multiplies the integer minor by the outer
   leading coefficient, covering degree drops as well as reducibility. For
   every full-outer-degree equation, its witness has logarithmic height at most
   27*d^4*(1+2*log(H)/d²), yielding the corresponding geometric prime charge.
   PlaneShear, LeadingDirection and ShearNormalization construct a parameter
   a in 0,...,d giving full outer degree. The shear is an integral polynomial
   automorphism, preserves total degree and irreducibility, commutes with
   arbitrary coefficient maps, and preserves the actual bad-prime set.
   ShearHeight bounds the transformed height by H*(d+1)^(d+2).
   GeneralBadReduction constructs a positive integer witness D with
     log D <= 189*d^4*(1+log(H)/d²),
   divisible by every geometric bad prime above d. At the cutoff 27*d^4,
   the charge is <= log(1+log(H)/d²)+log 7+2*mertensError+1.
   PlaneBadPrimes constructs the actual finite excluded set from D's prime
   factors and proves irreducibility of reductions outside it. This closes
   the coefficient-controlled bad-prime input for plane equations.
   Background for the differential criterion: Chen--Kayal--Wigderson,
   Partial Derivatives in Arithmetic Complexity (and beyond), section 15,
   https://www.math.ias.edu/~avi/PUBLICATIONS/MYPAPERS/CKW11/CKW11.pdf
   and Gao--Rodrigues, Irreducibility of polynomials modulo p via Newton
   polytopes, https://www.math.clemson.edu/~sgao/papers/GM01.pdf .
E. Combine the local divisibility exponents into a lower bound for the gcd
   of all maximal evaluation minors, retaining coefficient and degree control.
   SingularDeterminant now proves the logarithmic gcd lower bound for actual
   integral plane-curve points, including singular reductions. Its exact form
   retains denominators #X(F_p)+d^2(d-1), using the proved local divisibilities
   and multiplicity correction. Its prime-sum form assumes the actual
   #X(F_p)<=p+C*sqrt(p), irreducible reductions, and p>d outside an explicit
   excluded set B. The resulting error is
   (C+d^2(d-1))*primeErrorMass plus sum_{p in B} log(p)/p.
   PrimeCutoff now proves the actual prime tail
     sum_{p>L} log(p)/(p*sqrt(p)) <= 2*primeBlockMass/sqrt(L)
   for every finite prime set, by factor-four Mertens blocks. The resulting
   cutoff estimate charges log(L), and SingularDeterminantCutoff absorbs the
   singular correction above L>=d^4. At L=27*d^4 and prime upper endpoint s,
   singular_determinant_log_lower_at_rank proves
     log gcd >= s^2/2 * (log s - 4*log d - sum_{p in B} log(p)/p - K(C)),
   with K(C) independent of d. The actual sharp point-count bound
   #X(F_p)<=p+C*d^2*sqrt(p) and irreducibility at good primes remain hypotheses.
   The cutoff/degree-error analytic step is now closed. The finite-field
   estimate remains open. HeightDeterminant now constructs the excluded set
   and substitutes its height-controlled charge to prove
     log gcd >= s^2/2 * (log s - 4*log d - log(1+log(H)/d²) - K'(C)).
   The finite-field estimate is still a hypothesis; Proposition 3.2.6 for
   general curves is not yet proved.

Pinned Mathlib availability check (19 October 2026)
--------------------------------------------------
A source search at the pinned revision found no Weil/Hasse--Weil/Lang--Weil
curve-point bound or effective Noether-form/Ruppert bad-reduction theorem.
Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.SchwartzZippel supplies
MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_totalDegree, which gives at most d*q zeros for a
nonzero plane polynomial over a field of q elements. Its leading coefficient d
cannot replace the required q+C(d)*sqrt(q) estimate in the present determinant
argument. Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Projectivization.Cardinality counts ambient
projective space; NumberTheory.GaussSum develops character sums; and
AlgebraicGeometry.Geometrically.Integral supplies the geometric-integrality
property and base-change API. None of these inspected results discharges the
sharp finite-field obligation. The plane bad-prime input has since been
proved in this project by the differential construction above.

Then: projective auxiliary-polynomial degree (Theorem 3.1.1)
----------------------------------------------------------
The complete homogeneous monomial list and its binomial cardinality are now
proved in HomogeneousMonomials. HomogeneousHilbert identifies the entire degree-M
kernel of a principal homogeneous equation, giving the exact homogeneous Hilbert
function. HomogeneousRank proves the actual evaluation-rank inequality

    rank + binom(n+M-d, M-d) <= binom(n+M, M),  M >= d.

HomogeneousAuxiliary constructs independent spanning rows from an actual integer
equation and its zeros, then produces a nonzero homogeneous degree-M polynomial
vanishing at every supplied point with the exact Bombieri--Vaaler coefficient
bound. No monomial-list, rank-deficiency, or row-spanning hypotheses remain in
that theorem. The produced polynomial can still be a multiple of the equation.
HomogeneousRankDichotomy now clears denominators and proves that absence of
an integer auxiliary polynomial forces exact rational evaluation rank. For
plane curves the selected rank satisfies 2s+d^2=d(2M+3).
HomogeneousDeterminantComparison derives the leading-coefficient obstruction,
logarithmic gcd/Gram comparison, and archimedean box upper bound from that
absence hypothesis. PlaneChartDeterminant combines the actual chart x0=1 rows
with the singular lower bound, including its fourth-power cutoff form.
PlaneChartHeight now derives the bad-prime set and charge from absolute
irreducibility and the coefficient height. Only the sharp finite-field count
remains an arithmetic input to this comparison.
PlaneAuxiliaryDegree and PlaneAuxiliaryLargeHeight now derive explicit
logarithmic degree bounds from this comparison in the two height ranges.
PlaneAuxiliarySelection chooses the integer M and produces an actual integer
homogeneous nonmultiple, with no numerical threshold left to the caller:
  small-height: M <= d+log B+2*exp(K+23)*d^3*(1+log(H)/d²)*B^(2/d)/L^(1/d²)+2,
  large-height: M <= (34+8*exp(K+6+T))*d^3.
Here L is the absolute leading coefficient and K the determinant error. The
small range assumes log L<=4d log B; the large range assumes log H>=4d log B
and log H<=log L+T*d², with T>=0. Both still assume the sharp finite-field
point bound. The coefficient-position reduction is now proved:
IntegerGridInterpolation bounds coefficients from values at 0,...,d by
(d+1)^(d+1). PlaneGridHeight applies interpolation twice and constructs a
single plane-grid value controlling every coefficient by (d+1)^(2(d+1)).
HomogeneousTranslation and AffineTranslation lift the chart translation
integrally, preserve primitivity, homogeneity, chart degree and irreducibility
under arbitrary coefficient maps, and bound the new point box by (d+1)B.
HomogeneousLeadingCoefficient makes the chosen value the lexicographic
leading coefficient. HomogeneousEvaluationHeight and LeadingPositionHeight
bound the actual transformed coefficients using the factor
  P(d)=(d+1)^(4(d+1))*(d+2)^2*(2d+1)^d,
whose logarithm is at most 14d² for d>=1. The constructed coefficient height
H=P(d)*L is >=1 and satisfies log L<=log H<=log L+14d².
The scaled-model construction below now assembles this translation with both
degree/count branches and absorbs the height and box costs. The sharp
finite-field point count remains open.
PrimitiveIntegerPolynomial and PrimitiveNormalization now extract primitive
integer models of arbitrary nonzero rational equations, preserve degree and
homogeneity, and show that removing content does not increase coefficient
height. Primitive equations are relatively prime to every nonzero integer
constant; clearing denominators therefore reflects rational divisibility
without an irreducibility assumption.
HomogeneousChart proves injectivity on each homogeneous degree and constructs
bounded homogenization. When the chart preserves the equation's degree,
affine divisibility lifts to homogeneous divisibility. Primitive integer
homogeneous nonmultiples thus give proper rational affine sections.
PlaneAuxiliaryCount now applies Bezout to both height ranges and proves the
actual integer-box count forms. The small-height bound is d times the selected
auxiliary-degree bound, retaining B^(2/d); the large-height bound is
(34+8*exp(K+6+T))*d^4. These are not yet the B^(1/d) affine counting theorem.
This route must also handle irreducible but not absolutely irreducible inputs.

Then: affine plane counting (Proposition 4.2.1, Corollary 4.2.4)
-------------------------------------------------------------
Primitive normalization, bounded homogenization and the chart/divisibility
transfer are proved. PolynomialMapDeterminant and PolynomialMapAuxiliary now
extend the determinant and both auxiliary-degree branches to arbitrary
polynomial homogeneous-coordinate maps of the original plane points. The
original equation supplies the finite-field residue geometry; its scaled
homogeneous model supplies the leading-coefficient obstruction.
ScaledHomogenization constructs F_p with F_p(p,x)=p^d*f(x). A highest-degree
coefficient gains p^d, and all original coefficient sizes are retained.
ScaledHomogenizationPrimitive proves primitivity for p prime with p not
dividing f(0). HomogeneousSlice proves divisibility reflection on x0=p;
ScaledAuxiliaryCount therefore supplies actual proper rational sections and
the Bezout bound t<=d*M. ScaledModelCoordinates constructs the polynomial
map (p,x-a*p), bounds its radius by (d+1)B, and transports auxiliaries back.
ScaledModelPosition supplies bounded a and H>=p^d bounding the original
coefficients, with log L<=log H<=log L+14d². ScaledHeightElimination proves
the monotonicity needed to remove H. ScaledPlaneCount now combines these
actual constructions with both height branches. ScaledBoxExponent proves
  t <= K(C,A)*d^3*B^(1/d)*(log B+d)
when p is prime, B/A<=p<=B, p does not divide f(0), and the sharp finite-field
estimate holds with constant C. The constant K is explicit and independent
of the equation coefficients. No prime-existence assumption is hidden.
ScalingPrime now constructs the prime with absolute
A=exp(2*mertensError+2), assuming B>=A and log|f(0)|<B/A with f(0)!=0.
The proof uses the bounded-error first Mertens estimate and the prime-divisor
logarithmic charge; no prime-number theorem is assumed.
ScaledPlaneSmallCoefficient supplies the actual 1/d count in this branch.
The remaining analytic and translation cases are now proved:
UnscaledModelCount constructs a unit-scaled primitive model, applies both
auxiliary branches, and bounds points by O(d^4) when any actual coefficient
has logarithm at least 4d*log((d+1)B). AffineBoxRanges proves this threshold
is <=B/A once B>=(12A)^2*d^2, and bounds the unscaled 2/d expression on the
complementary small boxes. AffineNonzeroConstant combines these with Mertens
prime selection for every B>=1 when the constant term is nonzero.
AffineTranslationCount constructs a translation with parameters in 0,...,d
making that term nonzero. It preserves primitivity and actual residue counts
via an explicit equivalence over ZMod p. AffinePlaneAssembly absorbs its box
cost by curveBound(d,(d+1)B)<=2e*curveBound(d,B), proving the 1/d bound for
all primitive absolutely irreducible integer plane equations.
RationalPlaneAssembly clears denominators and content, obtaining the same
bound uniformly for rational absolutely irreducible equations. The only
counting hypothesis remaining here is SharpPlaneResidueBound C, explicitly
defined and still unproved. No coefficient-height, prime-existence or small-box
hypotheses remain in this assembled theorem.
PolynomialLinearDescent now sends a nonzero extension-field polynomial to a
nonzero base-field polynomial of no larger degree, preserving all base-field
zeros. NonabsolutePlaneCount partitions points between two nonunit factors
and applies Bezout to the two descended sections. This gives at most d^2
base-field points for an irreducible plane curve that splits over an extension,
without Galois transitivity or a smooth-point criterion. PlaneCurveAssembly
proves the exact PlaneCurveBound target from SharpPlaneResidueBound C for
C>=0, including all rational irreducible equations.
GeometricResidueReduction applies the same d^2 theorem over finite fields and
handles degree drops under reduction. It proves that
SharpGeometricPlaneResidueBound C implies SharpPlaneResidueBound C, so the
remaining point-count obligation concerns geometrically irreducible curves
only. The geometric sharp estimate is still an unproved proposition, not an
axiom. Prove it to discharge PlaneCurveBound unconditionally. The arbitrary-
curve theorem also needs the polynomial/filtered-degree interface.


Formal local and Stepanov machinery is now proved. FormalImplicitRoot constructs
and uniquely determines a formal simple root. FormalPlaneBranch constructs it
at a chosen nonsingular plane point. SectionImageRank extends the filtered
Bezout proof to arbitrary algebra-valued images. FormalBranchFaithful identifies
the formal branch kernel with (f), and FormalBranchOrder bounds a proper
section's vanishing order by d*m. PowerSeriesFrobenius proves that independent
jets of length p prevent cancellation with p-th-power coefficients.
FormalBranchMultiplicity combines distinct branches to bound N*#S by d*m.
FormalPlaneDifferentiation and PlaneTangentMultiplicity turn polynomial tangent
derivatives into actual local multiplicities, for N<=p.
PlaneFrobeniusAuxiliary proves nondivisibility and the point-count consequence
for auxiliaries sum(h_i*a_i^p). PlaneFrobeniusSystem constructs the a_i by a
finite linear kernel when the number of unknowns exceeds the summed filtered
dimensions of the constraints. PlaneStepanovBound chooses actual polynomial
bases and proves #S*N<=d*(D+p*A)+d*(d-1)*N under d*D<p, N<=p and
  sum(r<N,H(D+A+r*d)) < H(D)*H(A).
Here H is the actual principal-plane Hilbert function, already computed in
PlaneHilbert. Choose the integer parameters and prove the uniform numerical
inequality to obtain the sharp finite-field estimate. This last step is not
yet done; neither counting target is asserted unconditionally.


Completed: unconditional rational-plane theorem (19 October 2026)
----------------------------------------------------------------
StepanovParameters chooses A=floor(sqrt(p)/d), D=floor((p-1)/d), N=d*A-4*d².
For p>27*d^4 it proves d<=A,D, d*D<p, 0<N<=p, and the polynomial inequality
required by the finite linear system. PlaneStepanovDimension uses the exact
principal Hilbert function to verify the actual dimension inequality.
StepanovRealBound proves the real error estimate including all integer rounding:
  #S <= p + 161*d²*sqrt(p).
SharpPlaneCount proves this for every irreducible plane equation over ZMod p,
then proves SharpPlaneResidueBound 161 and PlaneCurveBound with no external
counting hypotheses. The preceding finite-field obligations are discharged.
The next obligation is the higher-dimensional projection and curve interface.

Then: arbitrary ambient dimension (Proposition 4.3.1)
---------------------------------------------------
Construct controlled integral projections preserving degree and birationality,
bound their exceptional fibers, and formalize the non-geometrically-integral
case. Relate the geometric degree to the target's filtered-coordinate-ring
definition. Track the constants so they depend only on ambient dimension.
Discharge AffineCurveBound without unproved hypotheses.


Completed projection algebra (19 October 2026)
---------------------------------------------
FunctionFieldRank uses independent powers of a transcendental linear coordinate
to bound the size of a parameter-field-independent polynomial family by d.
CurveFunctionField clears a common denominator, extending this to arbitrary
fraction-field elements, and proves the extension is finite of degree <=d.
CurveParameter proves that if every coordinate were algebraic, the quotient
would be finite-dimensional over the constant field, contradicting positive
linear Hilbert growth. CurveRationalParameter constructs the actual K(t)
embedding from one of the original coordinates.
BoundedLinearSeparation uses a product of univariate difference polynomials to
separate a finite vector family by coefficients (1,k,...,k^(n-1)), with
k<=n*card(family)^2. BoundedPrimitiveElement applies this to field embeddings;
it proves those embeddings are determined by the original affine coordinates.
CurvePrimitivePair therefore constructs an actual coordinate and integer linear
form generating the curve's function field, with k<=n*d². No parameter, finite
extension or coordinate-generation assumption is left over in this existence
theorem beyond the stated prime ideal and positive affine Hilbert degree.
BoundedProjectionCoordinates proves integral values and the box factor
1+n*(n*d²+1)^n. This is polynomial in d for fixed n.
The next stage below constructs the equation and a proper reconstruction
denominator. Degree preservation and the O(d²) exceptional bound remain open.


Plane projection equations and rational inverses (19 October 2026)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
LinearProjectionFiltration proves that linear substitution preserves the degree
filtration and that the image coordinate ring has no larger filtered dimensions.
PlaneProjectionKernel proves that the image kernel is nonzero and principal
when one projected coordinate is transcendental. PlaneProjectionDegree then
constructs an irreducible image equation of positive degree at most d.
PlaneIdealCount proves every prime plane ideal with positive affine Hilbert
degree d is generated by an irreducible equation of exactly degree d, giving
the unconditional n=2 instance of AffineCurveBound.
ProjectionFieldDegree proves that a primitive pair has image degree at least
the parameter extension degree. Thus a full-degree parameter suffices for
preservation of degree; its bounded existence remains to be proved.
PrimitivePairReconstruction and CurveRationalInverse turn field generation
into polynomial identities Q(a)*X_i=P_i(a) modulo the original ideal, with
Q(a) outside that ideal. BoundedBirationalProjection constructs such identities
for the actual bounded moment-coordinate pair. ProjectionExceptionalCount
proves injectivity away from Q(a)=0 and bounds the loss of points in any finite
source set by d*deg(Q). No degree bound for this constructed Q is claimed.
The next stage below proves the uniform exceptional-source-point bound for
any degree-preserving pair. The infinity construction below now also proves
bounded existence of such a pair.


Derivative reconstruction and uniform exceptional count (19 October 2026)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
PolynomialMatrixSpecialization clears a rational-function left inverse and
proves that an injective polynomial matrix is injective at an integer value.
PolynomialKernelOrigin clears denominators in a kernel vector and removes its
common power of X, producing a polynomial relation nonzero at zero whenever
all integer specializations have dependent columns. PolynomialKernelDerivative
also proves first-order lifting for a one-dimensional specialized kernel.
PolynomialCoefficientLinearMap and PolynomialFamilyRelations encode finite
families of algebra-valued polynomials using finitely many detecting linear
functionals. The target algebra need not be finite-dimensional.
CurveProjectionDeformation applies this to actual source curves: every linear
coordinate displacement has a plane relation of degree at most d, and there
is a polynomial family of such relations nonzero at zero. PlaneRelationSpace
identifies the initial relation as a scalar multiple of f when deg(f)=d.
PlaneLinearDeformation and PlaneDeformationRelation compute the first
coefficient. CurveDerivativeReconstruction then proves, for each linear source
function l, an identity f_Y(a)*l=P(a) modulo I with deg(P)<=d.
PlaneProjectionDerivative proves f_Y(a) is proper and deg(f_Y)<=d-1 when the
other projected coordinate is transcendental. DegreePreservingProjectionCount
therefore constructs one denominator for every source coordinate and proves
  #S <= #projection(S) + d*(d-1)
for every finite set S of source points. No normalization, absolute
irreducibility, point-count hypothesis or exceptional-fiber premise is used.
Degree preservation remains an explicit assumption of this theorem.
The bounded existence assumption is now discharged by the construction below.
The final integer-height/count assembly remains unfinished.

Bounded degree-preserving projection from infinity (19 October 2026)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
ParameterPowerSpan, RationalParameterPowerSpan and ParameterRecurrenceGrowth
bound filtered growth by the actual parameter-field extension rank.
CurveParameterFullDegree proves equality with the Hilbert degree when a linear
parameter generates the eventual filtration recurrence. CoordinatePowerGeneration
obtains that recurrence from balanced reductions of powers of all coordinates.
ProjectiveFiltration and InfinitySection construct the actual infinity quotient
and identify its stable graded dimension with d. RadialHomogeneousMap and
InfinityParameterReduction use the Nullstellensatz to obtain the balanced
reductions from infinity avoidance. RecurrenceParameterTranscendence rules out
an algebraic parameter using positive Hilbert growth; InfinityAvoidingProjection
constructs the parameter embedding and the full-degree second coordinate.
ScalarSpanDimension, InfinityEvaluationSpan and HomogeneousScalarExtension
control geometric evaluations over an extension field without assuming a
base-change Hilbert-degree result. HomogeneousChartInterpolation and
InfinityChartCardinality prove each normalized infinity chart is finite with
at most d points. InfinityScaling permits normalization. BoundedInfinityAvoidance
constructs a moment form nonzero on a finite family of nonzero vectors;
BoundedInfinityParameter applies it to all charts, giving k₀<=n²*d.
BoundedDegreePreservingProjection now proves, for every positive-degree prime
curve in characteristic zero, an irreducible plane equation of degree exactly d
for the two moment coordinates, with k₀<=n²*d and k₁<=n*d². It also proves
#S<=#projection(S)+d(d-1) for every finite source set. No geometric integrality,
external projection, supplied field embedding or exceptional-fiber hypothesis
is assumed. FullDegreePrimitiveProjection connects the recurrence proof to
the previously proved bounded primitive-element construction.
Complete affine counting assembly (19 October 2026)
---------------------------------------------------
DegreePreservingProjectionBox bounds both integral coordinates by H(n,d)*B,
where H(n,d)=(n+1)*((n+1)*(d+1))^(2*n). ProjectionScaleAbsorption proves
log H(n,d)<=(2*n²+3*n)*d and
  curveBound d (H(n,d)*B) <= exp(C_n)*(C_n+1)*curveBound d B,
where C_n=2*n²+3*n. AffineProjectionCount constructs one irreducible plane
equation of degree exactly d and proves the source count is at most its count
in the enlarged box plus d(d-1), simultaneously for every B>=1. The integer
and rational projection maps are proved compatible, including image cardinality.
AffineCurveBound.affineCurveBound now proves the complete AffineCurveBound
statement. It combines the unconditional plane theorem, the scale inequality
and d(d-1)<=curveBound d B. The constant is chosen before the source ideal,
degree and radius, and depends only on n. No external counting hypothesis,
projection, field embedding or geometric-integrality premise remains.

Pierce integration
------------------
The current joint-lift candidate proposes 128/435 and its powered optimization.
It needs n=7 for unpowered graph degrees 17 through 5928, and higher degrees
bounded in terms of fixed powers for the optimization. Exceptional curves
still need n=3 and degrees 2 through 24. It uses ordinary pattern counting.
The shared actual conic count is now proved in pierce-length-bound, but the
joint graph-degree lower bound remains a separate obligation; neither follows
from the results in this repository.

The full external input is now proved. After its integrated axiom audit,
pierce-length-bound can acquire a pinned dependency on this repository. This repository does not resolve the separate
Pierce resultant, geometry, or exceptional-pattern counting obligations.
